title: AMPLITUDE FOLLOWER -- smooth 0-1 envelope from live input

sections.heading: USING IT
lines: Listens to the left channel of the audio input (adc~). Turn on DSP to start.
smoothing (ms): how slowly the envelope rises and falls (1-5000, default 100).
floor (dB): the input level that reads as 0 (-96 to -6, default -60).
curve (S): shapes the response. 1 = straight; above 1 = S-curve; below 1 = inverse S.
input meter: the raw input level.
amplitude 0-1 (RMS/peak): the follower output, ready to use as a modulation source.
The output signal stops at the readout -- copy the gen~ into another patch to use it.

sections.heading: HOW IT WORKS
lines: A gen~ codebox tracks RMS level plus a scaled peak envelope and takes the larger.
The peak branch keeps noisy sounds from reading too low next to pitched ones.
A boosted high-pass branch (above ~1.2 kHz) makes hiss and 'sh' sounds read as loud as they feel.
The level is converted to dB, mapped from floor to 0 dB onto 0-1, then shaped by curve.
